nl.statement: A population BACKSHIFT multi-environment covariance system. Fix a dimension \(p\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\) and a finite label set \(E=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) of observed environment slots, a corruption budget \(c\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\), and \(h=m-c\). Write \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) and \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) for the real symmetric positive-semidefinite and positive-definite \(p\times p\) cones. An observed input is a family \(\Sigma=(\Sigma_e:e\in E)\in(\mathbb S_{+}^{p})^{E}\). A structural explanation consists of an invertible demixing matrix \(D\in\mathrm{GL}_p(\mathbb R)\) with connectivity target \(B=I_p-D\), an invariant disturbance covariance \(\Omega\in\mathbb S^{p}\) that is permitted to be nondiagonal and singular, and nonnegative diagonal intervention-variance levels \(s=(s_{ek})\) on an unknown honest set \(H\subseteq E\) with \(\lvert H\rvert=h\), linked by the equilibrium covariance equation \(\Sigma_e=D^{-1}(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e))D^{-\mathsf T}\) for \(e\in H\); the remaining \(c\) slots of \(E\setminus H\) may carry arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\). Admissibility is the BACKSHIFT normalization \(\mathcal D=\{A\in\mathrm{GL}_p(\mathbb R):\operatorname{diag}(A)=\mathbf 1,\ \operatorname{CP}(I_p-A)<1\}\), where \(\operatorname{CP}\) is the maximum absolute entry product along a directed simple cycle of length at least two. Two competing explanations \(D^{(1)},H_1,s^{(1)}\) and \(D^{(2)},H_2,s^{(2)}\) with \(\lvert H_r\rvert\ge h\) may share only the overlap \(J=H_1\cap H_2\), of size at least \(m-2c=h-c\). The geometry of a shift design is measured by affine lines \(L\subset\mathbb R^2\): the pairwise occupancy \(M_{k\ell}=\max_L\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\), the deletion distance \(\delta_H=\min_{k<\ell}(h-M_{k\ell})\), and the affine-minor separation \(\gamma_H\). The recovery map is the \(c\)-replacement compatibility set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\subseteq\mathcal D\), with its subset-enumeration presentation \(\text{SubsetConsensus}\). Conditioning margins are \(\kappa_D=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), \(\zeta_D=1-\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D)\), and the scale bound \(M_H=1+\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\); no interiority margin is imposed on the covariances, which are only required to be positive semidefinite. The size of a set-valued structural output is measured by \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}\), both valued in \([0,+\infty]\). — bypass-justified (ABSTRACTION MISMATCH against the whole declared cluster substrate root). The paper's ambient world carries no graph, no d-separation, no do-operator, no potential outcome, and no probability space at the population layer: an environment is a covariance matrix, an intervention is an unobserved diagonal variance shift, and identification is congruence-diagonalizer uniqueness under a normalization. Surveyed and rejected, one line each: `Causalean/Graph/SWIG.lean` + `Causalean/SCM/ID/GraphicalThms/*` (SWIG/d-separation graphical criteria; the paper never states a graphical condition and the target is a cyclic system, which `Graph/DAG.lean` forbids); `Causalean/SCM/ID/Identifiable.lean` and `Overlap.lean` (identifiability of an interventional kernel from an observational kernel by do-calculus; here the observable is a second-moment family and the target is a matrix, so `Identifiable`'s kernel-equality shape does not type-fit); `Causalean/SCM/Do/*` (do-calculus rules on measure kernels — no consumer); `Causalean/PO/**` and `Causalean/PO/ID/Exact/*` (`POSystem`, `Adjustment`, `Backdoor.*`, `Frontdoor.*`, `ATE.*`, `DID.*`, `DTR.*`, `LATE.*`, `*.Assumptions` — all are potential-outcome estimand identification under overlap/unconfoundedness; the paper has no treatment variable, no propensity, and no estimand of the form \(E[Y(a)]\)). What IS reused, and it is the highest-leverage reuse in this plan, is Causalean's linear-causal-discovery matrix layer, which sits at exactly this abstraction: `Causalean.Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.genPerm_of_det_ne_zero_of_colSupport` (Causalean/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/MonomialMatrix.lean:37) is verbatim the monomial-extraction step of `lem:overlap-uniqueness` ('invertibility then makes \(Q\) monomial'), and `Causalean.Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.perm_uniqueness` / `eq_of_genPerm_triangular_unitDiag` (:104,:132) are the unit-diagonal pinning template that the cycle-product argument replaces. A prespecified sparse intervention-design genericity world. On a probability space carrying the shift design, a deterministic binary support pattern \(Z\in\{0,1\}^{H\times p}\) is fixed before the experiment, and random positive amplitudes \(a\in(0,\infty)^{H\times p}\) produce the realized shift levels \(s_{ek}=Z_{ek}a_{ek}\). The joint law of the active subarray \((a_{ek}:Z_{ek}=1)\) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on its positive orthant; nothing is assumed about the inactive coordinates, and the amplitudes may be dependent. For each coordinate pair \(k<\ell\) the pattern determines the incidence counts \(n_{uv}^{k\ell}=\#\{e\in H:(Z_{ek},Z_{e\ell})=(u,v)\}\) and the closed-form generic occupancy \(M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}=\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},\ n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},\ n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\ \min(2,h)\}\). Points of type \(00\) coincide at the origin and are counted with their full multiplicity as indexed observations, so this is an incidence statement about an indexed family, not about a set of distinct points. — bypass-justified: this is a bare Lebesgue-genericity world, not a causal sampling world. Surveyed `Causalean/Stat/Sample.lean` (`IIDSample`), `Causalean/Stat/EmpiricalProcess/*`, `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/*` via `grep '^## '` of ../doc/API.md §12, §12ep, §12' and reads of the section tables: every Causalean sampling primitive is an i.i.d.-observation layer with empirical means and concentration, whereas this world has no observations and no estimator — it only needs `MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous` of one fixed law against the volume measure on a positive orthant and a null-set union over finitely many polynomial equations. Mathlib-side check for the one genuinely mathematical ingredient (`lean_leansearch` "zero set of a nonzero multivariate polynomial has measure zero" and "nonzero polynomial vanishes on a set of Lebesgue measure zero in R^n"): Mathlib supplies the univariate root finiteness `Polynomial.finite_setOf_isRoot` (Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Roots) and `MvPolynomial.support_nonempty` / `zeroLocus` algebra, but NO statement that the real zero set of a nonzero `MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ` is Lebesgue-null; Causalean-side check `grep -rln 'MvPolynomial' ../Causalean/` returns only `Causalean/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/PolynomialImageDimension/*` and `Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/MonomialGram.lean`, and `grep -n 'measure zero|Lebesgue|volume|addHaar'` over that directory returns nothing — that development is Zariski/dimension-theoretic and carries no measure. The gap is therefore a build-inline helper (`Helpers/PolynomialNull.lean`), proved by the induction the note's own proof spells out: expand in the last variable, apply the inductive hypothesis to the coefficient polynomials, and integrate the finite-root sections via `MeasureTheory.Measure.pi` / Fubini.

A set-theoretic finite-sample inference world layered on the population system. Fix a sample-size index \(n\geq1\) and a nominal noncoverage level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). For each slot \(e\in E\) the data supply an ARBITRARY nonempty simultaneous covariance region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\subseteq\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\); no representation, encoding, membership oracle, or computability property of a region is assumed, and no sampling mechanism producing it is specified. The honest-slot error radius is \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\), with the value \(+\infty\) permitted, and the identification-robust output is the confidence union \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}=\bigcup\{\mathcal R_c(\Gamma):\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\ \forall e\in E\}\), the union of the population replacement-compatibility sets over all simultaneous selections. The coverage event is \(G_{n,\alpha,H}=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\ \forall e\in H\}\). Quantitative statements are made against four fixed rational margins imposed on the TRUE instance — \(\gamma_H\geq\gamma_0\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\), \(\zeta_D\geq\zeta_0\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1]\), \(\kappa_D\leq\overline\kappa\in\mathbb Q\cap[1,\infty)\), \(M_H\leq\overline M\in\mathbb Q\cap[1,\infty)\) — together with a single declarative condition-number bound \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline\kappa\) on every feasible candidate. No covariance-interiority, candidate affine-separation, candidate normalization-slack, or candidate scale condition is imposed, and the local radius \(r_0\) is a non-effective compactness quantity: its existence is asserted, no procedure evaluates it, and no executable, algorithmic, or software interface is part of this world. — REVISED (core revision, whole-block rewrite): the previous S3 was an ENCODED-REGION world binding `RegionCode`, `lambda0`, `CertificateInferenceHandle` and `AuditedReleaseContraction`, and carrying a rational-semialgebraic syntax layer with a release/abstain certificate handle. The revised core deletes all four of those symbols and the entire symbolic layer: regions are now ARBITRARY nonempty subsets of \(\mathbb S_+^p\), the covariance-interiority margin is gone, and every executable/effective/decision/chart/software item is moved into the unresolved `oeq:certified-uniform-inference`. The whole `Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Basic` / `Mathlib.Data.Rat.Defs`-syntax module list, the `RationalSignFormula`/`FOFormula` plan, and the sibling-CAD analogous-module record are therefore DROPPED (they are recorded in `file_plan.bypass_survey` for provenance only). What remains is a plain `Set (Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ)`-indexed-family world over `ℝ≥0∞`-valued radii plus four rational margin parameters. bypass-justified (ABSTRACTION MISMATCH, re-surveyed for the revised world): Causalean's set-valued identification substrate is `Causalean/PO/ID/Partial/**` — `IdentifiedInterval`, support functions of random convex sets, and Hausdorff-distance vocabulary — which lives at the real-interval / convex-body abstraction over a potential-outcome estimand, whereas this world's uncertainty object is a family of arbitrary subsets of the PSD matrix cone and its output is a union of matrix solution sets. If \(\delta_H>c\), equivalently \(\gamma_H>0\), then \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every assignment of matrices in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). If, in addition, this fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) and \(\delta_H\le c\), then there are positive-definite values for all slots in \(E\setminus H\), a matrix \(D'\in\mathcal D\) with \(D'\ne D\), an invariant \(\Omega'\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), and nonnegative shifts on a set \(H'\subseteq E\) with \(|H'|=h\) such that \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\). nl.statement: The set-theoretic simultaneous-coverage implication for arbitrary nonempty positive-semidefinite covariance regions is established by \(\text{thm:confidence-union-coverage}\). Can one additionally build and formally verify an executable real-closed-field quantifier-elimination, sign-determination, and root-isolation substrate which, from finite rational-semialgebraic covariance-region codes, (i) terminates and emits a quantifier-free code whose realization is exactly \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\), (ii) decides a release-or-abstain condition, possibly using a conservative universal four-margin audit to certify unknown true-side margins and forcing abstention within that audit whenever it finds a feasible candidate with zero affine separation, while distinguishing that operational sufficient audit from the sole candidate-side condition-number bound required by the analytic contraction theorem, (iii) decides for every rational population covariance family whether \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) is empty, is a singleton, or contains at least two matrices, and (iv) computes a certified positive lower bound for the compact far-family residual and hence an effective positive radius \(r_0\)? Can the same verified program automate normalization-chart changes without altering the represented matrix set and support a corruption-aware extension of the CRAN \(\texttt{backShift}\) workflow? Every executable, effective, decision, chart-automation, and software item in this question is unresolved future work. A feasible candidate with zero affine separation or a small normalization slack may trigger that conservative operational audit, but neither is an analytic candidate-side obstruction to contraction around a fixed true instance satisfying \(\gamma_H\geq\gamma_0>0\) and \(\zeta_D\geq\zeta_0>0\).

nl.statement:
